CUSTOMER INSIGHTS / NLP

CASE STUDY / 04

Turning thousands of reviews into customer insight.

An academic NLP study of 10,000 app reviews, exploring written feedback through lexicon-based sentiment, supervised learning, and deep learning experiments.

01 / THE QUESTION

The business context.

App reviews contain useful customer feedback, but reading them all manually does not scale. This project investigates how review text can be organized into positive, neutral, and negative sentiment—and where the labeling and evaluation process needs care.

02 / EXPLORE THE WORK

FROM FEEDBACK TO UNDERSTANDING
Positive Neutral Negative
10,000Reviews explored
Conceptual text visualization

COMPARE THE APPROACHES

Same text. Different ways to learn.

Start with a sentiment lexicon

VADER scores the written review directly using a sentiment lexicon and rules. Star ratings are a comparison signal, not the input to VADER.

Method comparison based on the academic notebook. No live classifier or invented scores.

03 / THE APPROACH

From question to evidence.

01

Prepare

Cleaned, translated, tokenized, and lemmatized review text, with exploratory analysis of the dataset.

02

Score

Applied VADER to written text, using star ratings as a comparison rather than as VADER’s input.

03

Classify

Used TF-IDF text features with five traditional classification models and rating-derived sentiment targets.

04

Experiment

Explored LSTM and bidirectional LSTM text models as additional approaches.

04 / WHAT I LEARNED

The useful part of the analysis.

01

Text and ratings are different signals

A review’s star rating can disagree with its wording. Rating-derived targets are useful proxies, not independent ground truth.

02

Compare methods thoughtfully

The notebook explores lexicon-based, traditional ML, and deep learning approaches to the same text problem.

03

Improve validation first

Leakage-safe evaluation and reproducibility need further work before model scores can be fairly compared.

Customer insight requires attention to how labels are created, not just the model used to predict them.

05 / SCOPE & LIMITATIONS

What the evidence does—and doesn’t—say.

This presents the original academic notebook. Supervised targets were derived from ratings, while model inputs were review text. Final performance claims are omitted pending improved evaluation.
